mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 0.5 percentage points in the same month signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls by >0.5pp in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in real personal income (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a demand expansion, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-mo MA AND HOUST > 12-mo MA in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months signals an overheating labor market resolving into normalization, which supports stable wage growth and positive corporate margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) above 0.4% for six consecutive months signals robust consumer demand, which lifts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
